channel.title: LaunchDarkly incidents — Vendor Status Watch
channel.description: Incidents from LaunchDarkly's public status page, polled daily.

item.title: Flag delivery errors in Streaming API [resolved]
item.description: This incident has been resolved. Between 12:00 and 12:12 PM PDT on August 26, server-side SDKs establishing new streaming connections experienced elevated error rates. Existing streaming connections were not affected, and polling requests continued to be served with error rates below 1%. Some requests to the LaunchDarkly web application also experienced elevated errors between approximately 11:29 AM and 12:03 PM PDT. The issue was caused by an internal configuration change, which has been reverted. All systems have recovered and are operating normally. No customer data was lost or compromised.

item.title: Email delivery failure affecting sign-up verification and notification emails [resolved]
item.description:
Email delivery has been restored as of 2:32 PM UTC. Sign-up verification, password reset, teammate invitation, and notification emails are sending normally again.
We are re-sending sign-up verification and password reset emails that failed to deliver during the incident window (August 22, 11:48 PM CDT through today). If you attempted to sign up or reset a password during that period and haven't received an email within the next few hours, please retry the action or contact support.
We are continuing to monitor email delivery closely and will post a final update once we've confirmed sustained recovery.

item.title: Elevated API Latency and Errors (11:32–11:48 PT) [resolved]
item.description: Between 11:32 and 11:48 PT, customers experienced increased latency and elevated error rates on API endpoints. Latency and error rates have returned to normal, and the incident has been resolved.

item.title: Web application unavailable and flag delivery evaluations have elevated failure rate [resolved]
item.description:
All service availability has been fully restored.
Customers using server-side SDKs might need to restart their applications to re-enable the SDKs' connection to LaunchDarkly. Customers using the Relay Proxy may also need to restart their Relay Proxy; in this case, the Relay Proxy should be restarted before restarting their applications that connect to it.
To determine if an application needs to be restarted, customers can look at their application logs. Affected SDKs will emit (depending on language) logs containing one of "giving up permanently", "Invalid SDK key", "unauthorized", or "not authorized", or "401". Services which emitted logs such as these before 9:13AM PT may be unable to receive flag updates and will be unable to send events to LaunchDarkly until they are restarted.
